quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The heater in your rented flat has stopped working. Structure the email to your landlord; look at how precise the subject is.
options: Dear Mr Osei,
The heater in the living room stopped working on Sunday evening. Could someone come and look at it this week?

Kind regards,
Nina Petrova
Subject: Heater not working in flat 4B
quests.hint: If your landlord has many tenants, which subject would tell him where the problem is?
quests.explanation: Adding the flat number to the subject means the landlord knows who is writing and where the problem is, without opening the email. A subject like 'Problem' would waste his time.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You're the captain of a hockey team, and you need to tell teammates what to bring. Build the email.
options:
See you Saturday,
Chloe
Please bring your shin guards, a water bottle and a spare shirt. We'll meet at the school gate at 8 am.
Subject: Kit list for Saturday's tournament
Hi team,
quests.hint: Teammates are likely to search their inbox for this email later. Which subject will help them find it?
quests.explanation: Specific subjects are easier to find again. 'Kit list for Saturday's tournament' tells teammates the content and the date, so they can reopen the email on the morning of the match.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your college certificate hasn't arrived, and you are contacting the records office. Arrange the email.
options: Dear Records Office,
Subject: Certificate not received: Diploma in Design, 2024

Yours faithfully,
Theo Mensah
I completed the Diploma in Design last July but have not received my certificate. Could you check its status?
quests.hint: A busy office needs the course and year in the subject to route your email to the right person.
quests.explanation: In formal emails to large organisations, the subject often decides who reads the message. Naming the course and year lets the records office send it straight to the right staff member.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject and greeting are already written ('Subject: Question about the recipe' / 'Hi Auntie Rekha,'). Assemble the rest of the email.
options: Thanks so much!
Was it one teaspoon or two? I don't want to spoil it!
I'm making your lentil soup tonight and can't remember how much turmeric goes in.

Love,
Anil
quests.hint: Start with the reason you are writing, then ask the actual question.
quests.explanation: The first sentence should explain why you are writing. Here it gives context (making the soup), so the question that follows makes sense. Asking first would leave your aunt confused.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Extension for lab report / Greeting: Dear Dr Nakamura, / Arrange the body and closing of this student's email.
options:
Kind regards,
Amelia Ross
I am writing to ask whether I could have until Friday to submit my lab report.
I would be grateful for any flexibility you can offer.
I have been ill this week and missed two sessions.
quests.hint: The opening line should name the request. Reasons come after, not before.
quests.explanation: 'I am writing to ask whether...' tells the reader the purpose immediately. The reason then supports the request. If the illness came first, the lecturer would read it without knowing why it matters.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Wrong size delivered / Greeting: Dear Customer Care, / Arrange this short complaint about a shoe order.
options: I am writing about order 48213, which arrived today.

Yours faithfully,
Marcus Weber
I ordered size 41, but the box contains size 43.
Could you please arrange an exchange?
quests.hint: Anchor the message with the order first, then explain what went wrong.
quests.explanation: In customer emails, the order number in the first line helps staff open your record straight away. The problem comes next, and the request follows, so every sentence adds something new.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Study group on Thursday / Greeting: Hi all, / Arrange the message so the details are easy to follow.
options: Bring your notes and a highlighter.

Cheers,
Deepa
We're meeting to revise for the biology test.
It's on Thursday at 5 pm in Room 3 of the library.
quests.hint: Readers expect: what, then when and where, then what to bring.
quests.explanation: Details work best when they follow the questions your reader will ask: what is happening, when and where, and what should I do? Putting the equipment first would make people wonder what the meeting is for.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: New timetable for Year 9 / Greeting: Dear parents, / Arrange this notice from a school office.
options: This change lets us start lessons before the morning assembly.
From Monday, the school day will begin at 8:45 instead of 9:00.
Buses will arrive fifteen minutes earlier.

Yours faithfully,
The School Office
quests.hint: A notice states the change first, then the reason, then what the reader needs to know.
quests.explanation: Parents mainly want to know what changes. Explaining the reason helps them accept the change. The practical consequence (buses) comes last because it depends on the first two points.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Moving house / Greeting: Hi Ayesha, / Arrange this note from a friend who is moving to a new city.
options: I'll be back for your birthday, so we can celebrate together.

Miss you already,
Zoe
I got a job at a design studio there.
I have some big news: I'm moving to Glasgow in August.
quests.hint: Big news first, then why, then what it means for the friendship.
quests.explanation: Sharing news works well when you tell the headline first, follow with the reason, and end with what it means for the reader. This keeps a personal email warm and easy to follow.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject and greeting are done ('Subject: Can you come on Friday?' / 'Hi Kofi,'). Put together the body and sign-off.
options: Let me know if you can make it!
We're having a small barbecue at our house this Friday from 6 pm.
Some of the old football group are coming.

Cheers,
Dan
quests.hint: A closing sentence often tells the reader what to do next.
quests.explanation: A short line such as 'Let me know if you can make it!' shows the reader what response you expect. It comes after the details, and before the sign-off, so that it is the last thing they read.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Interview on Wednesday / Greeting: Dear Ms Green, / Arrange the confirmation from a job applicant.
options: I look forward to meeting you.
I am happy to confirm that I will attend.

Yours sincerely,
Leila Haddad
Thank you for inviting me to interview on Wednesday at 10 am.
quests.hint: Closing lines in formal emails often look forward to the next step.
quests.explanation: 'I look forward to meeting you' is a polite way to finish and signals that you are ready for the next step. It also works better than ending suddenly after the confirmation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Book club this month / Greeting: Hello everyone, / Arrange the reminder.
options: A quick reminder that our book club meets next Tuesday at 7 pm.
Please reply by Sunday so I can book a big enough table.

Best wishes,
Harriet
This month we are discussing 'Pachinko'.
quests.hint: Reminders should end with the action and the deadline for it.
quests.explanation: When a reply is needed, place the request and its deadline close to the end, right before the sign-off. Readers are more likely to remember the last thing they read.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Dentist appointment / Greeting: Dear Mr Yilmaz, / Arrange this appointment confirmation from a dental clinic.
options:
Kind regards,
Greenfield Dental
Your appointment is confirmed for Thursday, 12 June at 2:30 pm.
Please arrive ten minutes early to complete a short form.
If you cannot attend, call us at least 24 hours in advance.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence with the day, date and time. Where would a patient look first?
quests.explanation: The full date and time (weekday, date and hour) should appear early, because it is the reason the message exists. Giving both the weekday and the date helps readers notice a mistake.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Pizza night moved / Greeting: Hi Marta, / Arrange this message from a friend about a change of plan.
options:
Speak soon,
Danilo
Can we meet on Saturday, 21 June, at 7 pm instead of Friday?
I have to work late on Friday.
Sorry, but I need to change our pizza night.
quests.hint: Explain the change, then give the new date, and finally the reason.
quests.explanation: When plans change, give the new date in full ('Saturday, 21 June, at 7 pm') so the reader can put it in her diary at once. The reason is included after the request as a small courtesy.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Parents' evening / Greeting: Dear families, / Arrange this school message.
options: You can book a ten-minute slot through the school website.
Parents' evening will take place on Tuesday, 4 March.

Yours faithfully,
Mr Adeyemi, Head of Year
Appointments run from 4:00 pm to 7:00 pm in the main hall.
quests.hint: Event first, then the timing details, and finally how to take part.
quests.explanation: People plan around dates. Naming the event and date first lets readers decide if the email matters to them, and the booking instructions are last because they only matter if the reader plans to attend.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Swimming club for beginners / Greeting: Dear Coach Ahmed, / Arrange the enquiry from a parent.
options: Do you have any places for beginners this term?
Could you also tell me what the fees are?
My daughter is eight and would like to join your swimming club.

Kind regards,
Ruth Mbeki
quests.hint: Give the reader the context first. Then ask the main question, then the secondary one.
quests.explanation: Put the most important question first. If the coach answers only one, it should be the one you care most about. The context sentence makes both questions easier to answer.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Bus times to the airport / Greeting: Hi Ollie, / Arrange this message from a friend arriving by plane.
options: I'm landing at Manchester on Friday at 3 pm.

See you soon,
Julia
If not, I'll take a taxi, so please don't worry.
Do you know if there's a bus from the airport to your flat?
quests.hint: A friendly question can also include a small note that removes pressure.
quests.explanation: The last sentence keeps the question polite. It shows the friend he does not need to solve your problem, which makes an informal request feel considerate.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Opening hours on holidays / Greeting: Dear Museum Team, / Arrange the enquiry.
options:
Yours faithfully,
Paul Dubois
I am planning to visit your museum with a group of six adults.
If so, could you tell me what time the last entry is?
Will you be open on Monday, 5 May, which is a bank holiday?
quests.hint: The second question depends on the first answer. Put them in the order they logically follow.
quests.explanation: The last question only matters if the museum is open, so it comes second and is introduced by 'If so'. Questions that depend on each other should follow their natural sequence.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Re: Trip form / Greeting: Dear Mrs Ivanova, / Arrange this reply from a parent to a teacher.
options: Thank you for your email about the museum trip.
Please let me know if anything else is needed.
I have signed the form and my son will bring it on Monday.

Best wishes,
Carlos Vega
quests.hint: When replying, acknowledge the message you received before you give your answer.
quests.explanation: Starting with 'Thank you for your email' shows the reader you are responding to a specific message. The answer follows immediately, and an offer of more help comes last.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Re: Weekend plans / Greeting: Hi Ben, / Arrange your reply to a friend who suggested hiking.
options: I can't do the morning, but I'm free after 1 pm.
Hiking on Saturday sounds like a great idea!
Shall we go to the lake trail instead of the mountain?

Cheers,
Iris
quests.hint: React to the suggestion, then explain what works for you, and finally offer an idea.
quests.explanation: A good reply responds to the idea before adding conditions. Beginning with enthusiasm keeps the tone positive, and the counter-suggestion at the end moves the plan forward.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Re: Your enquiry about the piano course / Greeting: Dear Ms Alvarez, / Arrange the reply from a music school.
options:
Kind regards,
Helen Marsh, Music Academy
To reserve a place, please reply to this email by 25 August.
Thank you for your interest in our piano course.
The next beginners' class starts on 8 September and costs £120 for ten weeks.
quests.hint: In a service reply, answer the question first and explain the next step last.
quests.explanation: Businesses replying to an enquiry give the information the customer asked for, then tell them how to proceed. The deadline for reserving is placed last, so it is the final thing the customer sees.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Sorry about yesterday / Greeting: Hi Maya, / Arrange the apology to a friend you stood up.
options: My phone died, and I had no way of telling you.
I'm really sorry I didn't turn up at the cinema yesterday.

Sorry again,
Jakub
Can I make it up to you by buying the popcorn next time?
quests.hint: An apology has three steps: say sorry, explain briefly, and offer to put it right.
quests.explanation: A good apology accepts responsibility, gives a short reason, and offers something to repair the situation. A long explanation would sound like an excuse, so keep it brief.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Late submission of my essay / Greeting: Dear Professor Okafor, / Arrange the apology from a student.
options: I have attached the essay and will be more careful in future.

Yours sincerely,
Sophie Lambert
I apologise for submitting my essay two days late.
I misread the deadline and should have checked it more carefully.
quests.hint: In a formal apology, take responsibility before you refer to any attachment or the future.
quests.explanation: Formal apologies work best when the writer takes responsibility ('I should have checked') rather than blaming someone else. Promising to be more careful shows that the mistake will not happen again.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Apology for the noise / Greeting: Dear Mrs Baptiste, / Arrange the neighbour's apology.
options: We'll keep the volume down after 10 pm from now on.
We didn't realise the music could be heard through the wall.

Best wishes,
Kwame Boateng
I am sorry that our party kept you awake last Saturday.
quests.hint: Apology, then understanding, then a concrete promise.
quests.explanation: A promise with a specific limit (after 10 pm) is more convincing than 'we'll be quieter'. It gives the neighbour something they can check, which rebuilds trust.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You have just joined a book club and want to say hello. Assemble the email to the organiser, Harriet.
options:
Best wishes,
Priyanka
Dear Harriet,
Subject: New member: Priyanka Nair
I joined the book club this week and wanted to introduce myself. I love crime fiction, so I'm looking forward to the next meeting.
quests.hint: An introduction says who you are and why you are writing, then adds one personal detail.
quests.explanation: Introductions should be short. Name, connection to the reader and one interesting detail are usually enough. Adding your name to the subject helps the reader recognise you later.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are the new neighbour at number 9 and would like to say hello to Mr Sokolov. Lay out the email.
options: Dear Mr Sokolov,
We moved in last Saturday, and I wanted to introduce myself. My name is Tariq, and I live here with my wife and two children.

Kind regards,
Tariq Anwar
Subject: Hello from number 9
quests.hint: The subject should make the email feel friendly and easy to place.
quests.explanation: A friendly, informative subject encourages the reader to open the message. 'Hello from number 9' tells Mr Sokolov exactly who is writing, which is useful when you have never met.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are a new volunteer at an animal shelter. Arrange your first message to the volunteer coordinator.
options:
Thank you,
Kenji
Subject: New volunteer starting on Saturday
Hello Ms Ferrari,
I'm Kenji Sato, and I start as a volunteer this Saturday. Could you tell me what I should bring and where to meet?
quests.hint: Introduce yourself in one line, then ask what you actually need to know.
quests.explanation: An introduction that also asks a practical question works better than a bare 'hello'. The coordinator knows who you are and can reply with something useful.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are thanking your uncle for helping you move flats. Set out the email.
options:
Love,
Nia
Hi Uncle Raj,
Thank you for spending Saturday carrying boxes with me. I honestly couldn't have done it without you.
Subject: Thanks for helping me move
quests.hint: Read the relationship, then choose the warmth level of the greeting and closing.
quests.explanation: Review question: the email frame stays the same, but the tone follows the relationship. With family, 'Hi' and 'Love' are natural, and specific thanks (carrying boxes) sound sincere.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Absence on Monday / Greeting: Dear Mr Clarke, / Arrange the message from a parent explaining that their child will miss school.
options: She has a hospital appointment in the morning.

Kind regards,
Elif Demir
I am writing to let you know that Mia will be absent on Monday.
She will be back at school on Tuesday.
quests.hint: What happened, why, and when things return to normal: this order helps the teacher.
quests.explanation: Absence emails should be short and factual. The teacher needs the fact (absent), the reason and the return date. Extra details about the appointment are not needed.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Booking enquiry for a family room / Greeting: Dear Reservations Team, / Arrange the email to a hotel.
options:
Yours faithfully,
Lars Andersen
We would like to stay from 14 to 17 August.
Please also confirm whether breakfast is included.
Do you have a family room for two adults and two children?
quests.hint: State the dates before the questions, so that the hotel knows what to check.
quests.explanation: This review question combines several skills: specific details, a logical order and a formal tone. The hotel can only check availability once they know the dates, so those come first.
